name: JBM Auto Ltd
_note: Fact base, Rs crore unless stated. Every item carries src and published. Sources dated after 30-Sep-2026 were not used (Q2FY27 results and later filings ignored).

ar26.note: Annual report FY26, filed with the exchanges under cover letter JBMA/SEC/2026-27/33 dated 25-Aug-2026 (AGM 16-Sep-2026).

business.what: Flagship of the JBM group (founded 1983; JBM Auto incorporated 1996). Three reported segments: Component division (sheet-metal parts, chassis and suspension systems, fuel and air tanks, exhaust systems, skin panels, assemblies for car, utility-vehicle and truck makers), Tool Room (tools, dies and moulds) and the OEM division, renamed 'EV Business' in Q1FY27 (design, manufacture and sale of electric buses, spares, annual maintenance contracts and running of buses).
business.plants: 15 manufacturing facilities and a skill development centre (Crisil, Aug-2026); an integrated e-bus plant in Delhi-NCR with capacity of ~20,000 buses a year (AR FY26; IFC, Sep-2025).
business.customers: Components: Tata Motors, Mahindra & Mahindra, VE Commercial Vehicles and others (Crisil). Two customers above 10% of group revenue: Rs742 cr and Rs730 cr in FY26 (AR FY26 note 41). E-buses: state transport undertakings and city bus companies, mostly through the group's own GCC operator JBM Ecolife Mobility.
business.ebusUnits: ~1,282 e-buses sold in FY26, ~24% market share (AR FY26 MD&A); ~25% share in Q1FY27 (press release 30-Jul-2026). VAHAN registrations put JBM second in FY26 after Switch Mobility (press reports, Jun-2026): we note the conflict.
business.orderBook: Order book 'over 11,000 e-buses deployed and under execution' and Rs12,900 cr incl. 2,411 PM e-Bus Sewa buses (AR FY25); '10,000+ e-buses deployed and under execution' (Motilal Oswal deal release, 18-Jun-2026); Crisil (5-Aug-2026): 7,000-7,500 buses to be executed over 2-3 years. ~3,400 JBM e-buses deployed in India; ~5,000 expected within 12 months (Jun-2026).

structure.jbmev: JBM Electric Vehicles Pvt Ltd: 85% subsidiary (AR FY26 note 37) that holds the e-bus manufacturing; minority 15%. Its JVs JBM Green Energy Systems (batteries) and JBM EV Industries are equity-accounted.
structure.ecolife: JBM Ecolife Mobility Pvt Ltd: the GCC operating platform (buses leased to cities under gross-cost contracts in project SPVs). JBM Auto owns 83% but it is a joint venture (joint control with investors), equity-accounted; its 12 project SPVs are its subsidiaries. Investors include ADB and AIIB (US$100 mn; press reports), IFC (US$100 mn, 11-Sep-2025), Motilal Oswal Alternates (Rs750 cr of CCDs and NCDs, 18-Jun-2026).
structure.jvLosses: Share of JV losses: Rs35.5 cr (FY25), Rs31.8 cr (FY26), Rs7.9 cr (Q1FY27). Equity-accounted carrying value of JV investments Rs59 cr (Mar-26) after losses absorbed up to the carrying amount for Ecolife.
structure.exposure: At Mar-26 JBM Auto had lent Rs336 cr to JBM Ecolife (10.5%, 3 years), held Rs302 cr of 8% preference shares in it, given Rs86 cr of corporate guarantees for it and Rs224 cr for its Odisha SPV, bank guarantees for its SPVs, and pledged its Ecolife shares against Ecolife's borrowings (AR FY26 note 40/41). Ecolife Green One Mobility (100% subsidiary, a GCC SPV) is consolidated. Crisil fully consolidates Ecolife Green One and 'moderately' consolidates the other GCC SPVs because of the guarantees.

q1fy27.segments: Components Rs894.1 cr (+15.5%), EBIT Rs69.4 cr; Tool room Rs89.2 cr, EBIT Rs14.8 cr; EV business Rs460.0 cr (+16.7%), EBIT Rs48.6 cr.
q1fy27.highlights: ~25% e-bus market share; JBM Ecolife's Rs750 cr investment from Motilal Oswal Alternates; agreement with DRIVN (an electric commercial-vehicle leasing platform) for 500 electric luxury buses; long-term debt cut by ~Rs500 cr; JBM Galaxy sleeper/seater electric coach launched; fleets flagged off in Ahmedabad (155), Vadodara (130), Delhi (110), Panipat (70), Gandhinagar (40), Jamnagar (25), Ambala (20).
q1fy27.board: Board approved raising up to Rs1,500 cr through securities (QIP or other routes), subject to shareholders (30-Jul-2026); a similar Rs1,500 cr enabling resolution was passed at the Sep-2025 AGM and not used.

guidance.crisil: Crisil (5-Aug-2026, rating A/Stable reaffirmed): revenue to grow 14-16% a year over the medium term; operating margin ~12% in FY26 to improve 50-60bp; bus segment to exceed 40% of revenue in 1-2 years (36% in FY26); non-GCC (private) buses to rise from 12% of bus sales to over 25%; debt Rs3,204 cr at Mar-26, Rs2,500-2,550 cr by Mar-27; debt/EBITDA from 4.5x (FY26) to ~3x (FY27); interest cover from 2.2x to ~3x; gross current assets 297 days (Mar-26) to ~250 days (Mar-27) and 230-240 days later; cash accrual Rs450 cr (FY27) and Rs455-500 cr a year after; capex Rs100-150 cr a year; debt repayments Rs300-350 cr a year.
guidance.management: JBM Auto holds no earnings calls (none listed on Screener; no transcript found). Management statements come from press releases: '~5,000 e-buses on roads in the next 12 months' (18-Jun-2026) and the e-bus order book.

balanceSheet.mar26: Borrowings Rs3,029 cr (Screener: long-term Rs937 cr, short-term Rs2,070 cr, leases Rs23 cr); cash Rs130 cr; investments Rs409 cr, of which Rs302 cr are preference shares in JBM Ecolife, Rs23 cr in JBM Green Energy and Rs59 cr equity-accounted JVs. Trade receivables Rs2,185 cr (Rs1,007 cr a year earlier; Rs366 cr overdue 6-12 months); contract assets (unbilled revenue) Rs1,511 cr (Rs1,126 cr); loan to the JV Rs336 cr; trade payables Rs1,702 cr.
balanceSheet.proForma: We move Rs410 cr from working capital to net cash in the Mar-26 base for the Jun-2026 upstreaming (Crisil: Rs400-420 cr; assumptions.json otherTreasury).

accounting.revenueRecognition: Bus sales are recognised over time, by the share of total expected costs incurred (input method), not on delivery (AR FY26 note 47). Tooling revenue too. This is why contract assets (work done, not yet billed) reached Rs1,511 cr at Mar-26.
accounting.relatedSales: A large share of e-bus sales goes to JBM Ecolife and its SPVs, a JV that JBM Auto funds with loans, preference shares and guarantees. The related-party note in the AR is printed as rotated tables that our extraction could not read reliably; we do not quote a figure (see gaps).
accounting.auditor: Statutory auditor Marwah & Co. LLP (unmodified opinion on FY26).
accounting.exceptional: FY26 exceptional charge Rs9.7 cr (Q3FY26, new labour codes).
accounting.otherIncome: FY26 other income Rs138.9 cr: interest Rs92.4 cr, miscellaneous Rs35.7 cr, royalty Rs4.0 cr, rent Rs3.4 cr, subsidy Rs1.9 cr, other Rs1.5 cr (AR FY26 note 29). FY25 Rs53.6 cr.

management.md: Nishant Arya, Vice-Chairman and Managing Director (son of the Chairman; director since Jul-2009); led the group's move into buses and renewables. Re-appointed as MD at the Sep-2026 AGM (special resolution).
management.others: Dhiraj Mohan (whole-time director), Vivek Gupta (CFO), Sanjeev Kumar (company secretary).
management.rpt: Shareholders approved material related-party transactions with Neel Metal Products (promoter-group) of up to Rs1,000 cr a year (Sep-2025 AGM) and further material related-party transactions by postal ballot (Dec-2025). NSE sought clarification on price/volume movements several times in FY26 and on an XBRL error in the Q2FY26 results (secretarial audit).

corporateActions.what: JV with Solaris Bus & Coach (Poland) to make electric buses in India (JBM Solaris Electric Vehicles appears as a JV in the FY21 AR).
Entry into e-bus manufacturing (Crisil). OEM-division revenue Rs239 cr in FY20, Rs459 cr in FY21 (AR FY21).
Share split from Rs2 to Re1 face value (shareholders' approval 26-Dec-2024): 23.65 cr shares.
JBM Ecolife wins 1,021 e-buses (~Rs5,500 cr over 12 years) under PM e-Bus Sewa-2 in 19 cities of Gujarat, Maharashtra and Haryana.
IFC invests US$100 mn in JBM Ecolife Mobility for e-bus deployment.
Motilal Oswal Alternates invests Rs750 cr in JBM Ecolife (CCDs and NCDs); Rs400-420 cr upstreamed to cut JBM Auto's debt.

Press report of Bain Capital talks for a ~US$300 mn stake in the EV business; JBM Auto told the exchanges that JBM Electric Vehicles 'continuously evaluates routine fundraising options' and that no binding agreement had been signed.
